finding.claim: Any authenticated user can drop tables via /admin/drop because the Authorize result is discarded.
finding.source: Authenticated request with any role; the request must carry a *User in context (set by middleware not present in this directory).

trace.note: u := userFrom(r) retrieves the user from request context
Authorize(u, "dba") is called but its error return is ignored, so the check has no effect
r.FormValue("t") is concatenated into a DROP TABLE statement and passed to runSQL
Handler returns 204, so the drop succeeds silently for non-DBA users

finding.guards_checked: Authorize (api.go:13-20) is correct in isolation but ineffective at this call site because its error is ignored. No table-name allowlist, no HTTP method check, no CSRF check on this path.

verdict.guard_found: Authorize (api.go:13-20) exists and would return "forbidden" for non-dba users, but its result is discarded by a bare call at api.go:26, so it blocks nothing. The vacuum handler (api.go:33-36) checks the error correctly, which shows the intended dba-only control was omitted from dropTable. No table-name allowlist or parameterization exists between r.FormValue("t") (api.go:27) and runSQL. No method or CSRF check exists on this path.
verdict.reason: Authorize's error is discarded at api.go:26, so any authenticated non-dba user reaching /admin/drop (api.go:44) gets the unparameterized "DROP TABLE " + r.FormValue("t") at api.go:27 executed, and the handler returns 204 at api.go:28. The attacker needs only a valid *User in context, which the candidate states is set by middleware outside this directory.

finding.claim: SQL injection via the unvalidated table name parameter t in DROP TABLE.
finding.source: r.FormValue("t") at api.go:27 (query string or form body, fully attacker-controlled).
finding.sink: runSQL("DROP TABLE " + t) at api.go:27; runSQL (api.go:41) is a stub, assumed to execute its argument as SQL.

trace.note: Raw form value is concatenated into a SQL string with no identifier validation or quoting
runSQL is a stub; assumed to execute the string as SQL

finding.guards_checked: None on this path. Table identifiers cannot be parameterized, so the fix requires an allowlist of table names. Remains exploitable after fixing F1 by any role that passes the authorization check.

verdict.guard_found: Authorize(u, "dba") at api.go:26 is a bare call whose error return is discarded, so it blocks nothing. No identifier allowlist, quoting, or parameterization exists between r.FormValue("t") at api.go:27 and runSQL. The only check that works is the if-err guard in vacuum (api.go:33-35), which is not on the dropTable path.
verdict.reason: The attacker is any caller who reaches /admin/drop with a user in context (userFrom at api.go:22 panics otherwise), since the Authorize result at api.go:26 is discarded, and r.FormValue("t") is concatenated unvalidated into the SQL at api.go:27. The one caveat is that runSQL at api.go:41 is an empty stub, so the injection is real only once runSQL executes its argument as SQL, as the candidate assumed. The candidate's guard note that exploitation requires a role that "passes the authorization check" is wrong, because the check's result is never tested.

finding.claim: Admin endpoints use a state-changing GET-accessible path (CSRF risk) and bind plain HTTP on all interfaces (cleartext exposure). Needs verification against code outside this directory.
finding.source: Query string or form parameter t on /admin/drop (api.go:27); network clients reaching port 8083 (api.go:46).
finding.sink: Destructive DROP TABLE via /admin/drop (api.go:44, 27); cleartext admin traffic and any credentials on :8083 (api.go:46).

trace.note: /admin/drop is registered on the default mux with no method restriction or auth wrapper visible in this file
Parameter is read via FormValue, which accepts query-string values, so a link or image can trigger the action
http.ListenAndServe(":8083", nil) binds all interfaces over plain HTTP with no TLS

finding.guards_checked: No method check, CSRF token, or TLS in this file. The auth middleware that sets the "user" context key is not in this directory, so production protection cannot be confirmed.

verdict.guard_found: Authorize(u, "dba") at api.go:26 is the only in-handler control, but it is a bare statement whose error return is discarded, so it never blocks. The /admin/vacuum handler at api.go:33-36 checks the error correctly, which shows the intended pattern. No method check, CSRF token, or TLS exists in this file. The auth middleware that sets the "user" context key is outside this directory and cannot be verified. Parameter t is concatenated into SQL with no allowlist at api.go:27.
verdict.reason: The trace lines all match the code (route registration at api.go:44, FormValue at api.go:27, plain-HTTP ListenAndServe on :8083 at api.go:46), and the role check at api.go:26 is a discarded return value, so any user who passes the external auth middleware can run DROP TABLE on the attacker-chosen name at api.go:27, including via a GET link or image if the session is cookie-based.
